words.meaning: Saw or noticed something carefully.
Short, thick plants with many branches.
Small differences in amount, type, or level.

medium.simple_explanation: Small differences or changes between things of the same type.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when you try to draw a circle and end up with ten variations of a lumpy potato.

My morning hair has many variations of messy depending on which way I rolled in my sleep.

words.meaning: To form a picture in the mind.

words.meaning: Takes up a specific space or position.

words.meaning: A range of many different things.

words.meaning: A group of plants or animals living together.

words.meaning: Increased in size or developed naturally.

hard.funny_explanation: A forest that has never seen a selfie stick, a hiking boot, or a plastic wrapper.

hard.real_world_analogy: A family secret recipe that only your grandmother knows and never leaves her kitchen.

words.meaning: Naturally belonging to a certain place; not from outside.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To describe species that originate naturally in the local region.

hard.funny_explanation: The 'local' person who knows exactly where the best street food is without using Google Maps.

examples.text: Neem is an indigenous tree species of the Indian subcontinent.
My laziness on Sunday mornings is indigenous to my personality.

hard.real_world_analogy: A homemade meal made entirely with ingredients grown in your own backyard.

hard.simple_explanation: Coming from a foreign country; not native to the local environment.
hard.funny_explanation: That one cousin who lives abroad and returns with a fancy accent and weird clothes after just one week.

examples.text: Eucalyptus is an exotic species introduced to India from Australia.

words.meaning: Recognized or named based on specific features.

My mom instantly identified the 'mystery smell' as my old gym bag hidden under the bed.

words.meaning: Trees that shed their leaves every year.

I'm like a deciduous tree in the winter—I lose my pencils, my homework, and my patience.

hard.simple_explanation: All the plant life present in a particular region or time period.
hard.funny_explanation: Nature's department of 'Green Things That Just Stand There and Look Pretty.'

words.meaning: A specific area or part of a country.
The total animal life of a particular region.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: To provide the scientific term for the animal life of a region.
hard.simple_explanation: All the animal life of a particular region or time period.
hard.funny_explanation: The 'Moving Parts' of the forest that usually run away or try to eat you when you get close.

hard.real_world_analogy: The guests at a party who move around, talk, and eat all the snacks.

words.meaning: Limited to certain areas or conditions.

medium.simple_explanation: Kept within certain limits or only found in specific areas.
medium.funny_explanation: Like being grounded to your room; you can't just wander wherever you want, you are stuck in one spot!

My access to the cookie jar is strictly restricted by my mom's 'no dessert before dinner' rule.

words.meaning: Water falling from the clouds as rain.

The distance from top to bottom.
A particular area or part of the world.
Having a pleasant amount of heat.
Growing thickly, strongly, and healthily.

hard.simple_explanation: Growing thick, healthy, and in great abundance.
hard.funny_explanation: Like a shampoo commercial for a forest where every plant has perfect, thick hair.

hard.real_world_analogy: A buffet table overflowing with so much food you can't even see the tablecloth.

words.meaning: Plants considered as a whole.

medium.funny_explanation: Think of it as nature's giant, unchopped salad growing right out of the ground.

If I don't mow the lawn for a month, the vegetation in our backyard looks like a miniature jungle.

medium.funny_explanation: The 'middle child' of the plant world—too tall to be grass, but too short to be a tree.

The neighbor’s cat likes to hide in the shrubs and jump out like a tiny, furry ninja.

hard.funny_explanation: Like a giant forest sandwich with trees as the bread, shrubs as the cheese, and creepers as the mayo.

words.meaning: The way something is built or organized.

medium.simple_explanation: The way in which parts are arranged or put together to form a whole.
medium.funny_explanation: Like a giant LEGO set made of leaves and branches, organized into different floors.

examples.text: The different heights of plants give the evergreen forest a multilayered structure.
The structure of my triple-decker sandwich failed when the tomato slid out the side.

words.meaning: Clearly stated or decided; certain.

medium.funny_explanation: When your teacher says there is a 'definite' test on Friday, it means there’s no escaping it!

words.meaning: To lose leaves naturally at a certain time.

I tried to shed my responsibility for the broken vase by blaming the ghost in the attic.

words.meaning: Related to buying and selling for profit.

hard.simple_explanation: In a way that relates to buying, selling, or making a profit.
hard.funny_explanation: When a tree stops being a home for squirrels and starts being a paycheck for humans.

hard.real_world_analogy: The difference between growing a tomato in your garden for fun and owning a massive farm that sells them to supermarkets.

words.meaning: A large amount or more than enough.

hard.funny_explanation: Trees that decide they are tired of their clothes once a year and throw them all on the floor.

words.meaning: Found or distributed over a large area.

hard.funny_explanation: Nature's giant bathtub faucet that gets turned on full blast for a few months.

words.meaning: Being able to be used or obtained.

hard.real_world_analogy: Checking if there are any seats left on a bus before you try to get on.

words.meaning: Slightly wet or damp.

words.meaning: Most important, powerful, or common.

words.meaning: Continuous areas of land or water.

hard.funny_explanation: Forcing the ground to give you food instead of just letting it grow random weeds.

words.meaning: Very bright or colorful.
The feathers that cover a bird's body.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Specifically describes the colorful feathers of the flamingo birds in the Rann of Kachchh.
hard.simple_explanation: The entire layer of feathers that covers a bird.
hard.funny_explanation: A bird's high-fashion, all-weather outfit that it can never take off.

examples.text: The peacock displayed its magnificent plumage to attract a mate.
The pigeon looked very proud of its gray plumage, even if it was just covered in city dust.

hard.real_world_analogy: A natural, built-in tuxedo or evening gown for birds.

words.meaning: Very unusual, special, or remarkable.

medium.simple_explanation: Very unusual, remarkable, or special.
medium.funny_explanation: It sounds like 'extra' ordinary, but it actually means the opposite—it's super weird or super cool!

examples.text: Seeing thousands of flamingos in one place is an extraordinary sight.
It was extraordinary how my cat managed to eat my homework and the dog's dinner at the same time.

words.meaning: Things passed down from older generations.

medium.simple_explanation: The traditions, achievements, or natural wonders handed down from the past.
medium.funny_explanation: It’s like a giant 'hand-me-down' from your ancestors, but instead of an old sweater, it’s a whole planet.

examples.text: We must protect our natural heritage for the survival of future generations.
My family heritage consists mostly of a secret recipe for slightly burnt toast.

words.meaning: Relating to the scientific study of plants.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Refers to the specialized gardens funded by the government to study and preserve plant species.
hard.simple_explanation: Related to the scientific study of plants.
hard.funny_explanation: A fancy way of saying 'it’s all about the leaves, roots, and seeds.'

examples.text: The city's botanical garden contains rare flowers from across the globe.
My botanical skills are so bad that I once accidentally 'ended' a plastic plant.

hard.real_world_analogy: A museum, but instead of old statues, it's full of living, breathing plants.

words.meaning: Safe places where animals are protected.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Describes the 573 protected areas set up to provide a safe home for wildlife.
hard.simple_explanation: Safe places where wildlife is protected from hunting and danger.
hard.funny_explanation: The animal equivalent of a VIP lounge where 'No Humans Allowed' is the main rule.

examples.text: Wildlife sanctuaries play a vital role in preventing the extinction of rare species.
My bedroom is my personal sanctuary where no chores are allowed to enter.

hard.real_world_analogy: A safe room in a house where you go to hide when everything outside is chaotic.

words.meaning: The state of continuing to live or exist.
Done at random without careful thought.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Warns against the random, non-selective destruction of the environment.
hard.simple_explanation: Done at random or without making a careful choice or distinction.
hard.funny_explanation: Like trying to kill a fly on the wall with a sledgehammer; you get the fly, but you lose the wall too.

examples.text: The indiscriminate use of chemical fertilizers can harm the soil over time.
He was so indiscriminate with his party invites that even his mailman and a random cat showed up.

hard.real_world_analogy: Throwing a giant bucket of paint at a wall instead of using a tiny brush to paint a specific flower.

words.meaning: The act of damaging something beyond repair.
Different choices or options available.

medium.simple_explanation: Different choices or options you can pick from.
medium.funny_explanation: Like having to choose between pizza or burgers—both are great, but you can only pick one for the answer sheet!

examples.text: Choose the right answer from the four alternatives provided in the question.
The alternatives were to finish my chores or lose my phone; it wasn't much of a choice!

words.meaning: Cold, treeless region found in Arctic areas.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It is listed as a specific type of vegetation found in extremely cold regions.
hard.simple_explanation: A vast, flat, treeless Arctic region where the subsoil is permanently frozen.
hard.funny_explanation: Imagine the Earth's giant outdoor freezer where the grass is too scared of the cold to grow tall.

examples.text: Mosses and lichens are the primary vegetation found in the Tundra.
I tried to plant a mango tree in the Tundra, but it turned into a popsicle in five minutes.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a sports field that has been covered in ice for a thousand years.

words.meaning: Related to the rising and falling of the sea.

medium.simple_explanation: Relating to the rise and fall of the ocean's water levels.
medium.funny_explanation: The ocean's way of doing 'the wave' at a stadium, but it takes all day and happens twice.

examples.text: Tidal forests are found in areas influenced by the sea's high tides.
My sandcastle was destroyed by a tidal surge that I definitely didn't see coming.

words.meaning: Hot and humid regions near the equator.

medium.simple_explanation: Relating to the warm, humid regions near the Earth's equator.
medium.funny_explanation: A place where the sun treats every day like a beach party and the humidity makes everyone's hair go 'poof'.

examples.text: Tropical evergreen forests stay green throughout the year due to high rainfall.
I tried to dress for a tropical climate but ended up looking like a walking pineapple.

words.meaning: Trees that stay green all year round.
A tropical tree used to make medicine.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The book asks about the habitat of these trees, which are economically and medicinally important.
hard.simple_explanation: A tropical tree whose bark is used to make quinine, a medicine for malaria.
hard.funny_explanation: The 'Doctor Tree' that tastes like bitter medicine but saves you from itchy mosquito fever.

examples.text: Cinchona trees thrive in areas with rainfall exceeding 100 cm.
If mosquitoes had a 'Most Wanted' list, the Cinchona tree would be at the top.

hard.real_world_analogy: It is like a natural pharmacy growing in the middle of a rainy forest.

words.meaning: The amount of rain that falls.
Protected area for conserving nature and wildlife.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The chapter discusses conservation areas like Simlipal that protect biodiversity.
hard.simple_explanation: A large protected area meant for the conservation of wildlife, plant life, and traditional human lifestyles.
hard.funny_explanation: A giant 'No Humans Allowed to Mess Around' zone where animals get to live their best lives.

examples.text: Simlipal is a famous bio-reserve located in the state of Odisha.
In a bio-reserve, the tigers are the landlords and humans are just temporary visitors.

hard.real_world_analogy: It’s like a high-security gated community, but for tigers, birds, and rare flowers.

words.meaning: To be in a particular place.
Using only a few words; quickly.

medium.simple_explanation: Using only a few words to explain something quickly.
medium.funny_explanation: The exact opposite of how your parents explain why you need to eat your vegetables.

examples.text: The teacher asked the students to answer the geography questions briefly.
I briefly considered sharing my candy, but then I ate it all myself.

words.meaning: Specific things used to explain a rule.
To recognize the difference between two things.

medium.simple_explanation: To recognize or point out the differences between two or more things.
medium.funny_explanation: Being able to tell the difference between a real tiger and your cat wearing a striped sweater.

examples.text: Can you distinguish between flora and fauna in this ecosystem?
It is hard to distinguish my brother's messy room from a literal disaster zone.

words.meaning: All the plant life in a region.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to categorize the plant life of India as part of the country's natural heritage.
hard.simple_explanation: All the plant life present in a particular region or time.
hard.funny_explanation: Basically, the 'Green Gang' of a place—everything that stays rooted and does photosynthesis.

examples.text: The Himalayan region has a very diverse flora ranging from oaks to rhododendrons.
My garden's flora consists mostly of weeds and a very confused cactus.

hard.real_world_analogy: Flora is the wallpaper and furniture of nature's house.

words.meaning: All the animal life in a region.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used alongside flora to describe the total biological wealth of India.
hard.simple_explanation: All the animal life of a particular region or time.
hard.funny_explanation: The 'Moving Crew' of the forest—anything that walks, crawls, flies, or swims.

examples.text: India’s fauna includes the majestic Royal Bengal Tiger and the Asiatic Lion.
The fauna in my kitchen usually includes a very fast cockroach and a sleepy cat.

hard.real_world_analogy: Fauna are the actors and residents living inside nature's house.

words.meaning: Trees that shed leaves every year.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It identifies a major type of forest in India that sheds leaves seasonally.
hard.simple_explanation: Trees or shrubs that shed their leaves annually at the end of the growing season.
hard.funny_explanation: Trees that decide to go completely bald once a year just to save some water.

examples.text: Teak and Sal are common trees found in tropical deciduous forests.
Deciduous trees are like people who take off their clothes when it gets a little dry outside.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a person who switches their heavy winter coat for a light t-shirt, or vice versa, every year.

words.meaning: Large areas covered mostly with trees.
A group of similar living things.

medium.simple_explanation: A specific group of similar living things that can breed with each other.
medium.funny_explanation: A massive family tree where everyone actually looks like they belong together.

examples.text: Many species of plants in India are unfortunately becoming endangered.
I think my dog is a rare species of 'couch potato' that only wakes up for snacks.

words.meaning: At risk of disappearing or becoming extinct.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The book discusses why certain species are at risk of disappearing in India.
hard.simple_explanation: A species that is very likely to become extinct in the near future.
hard.funny_explanation: Animals that are down to their last few lives and really need a 'Save Game' button.

examples.text: The Red Panda is an endangered species found in the high-altitude forests.
My phone battery is endangered; it's at 1% and the charger is in the other room!

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a limited-edition sneaker that is no longer being manufactured.

words.meaning: Traditions or features passed down through generations.

medium.simple_explanation: Something like traditions or nature that is passed down from previous generations.
medium.funny_explanation: The cool stuff we got from our ancestors that we promise not to break or lose.

examples.text: India has a rich heritage of diverse flora and fauna.
My family heritage includes a secret recipe for spicy pickles and a very loud laugh.

words.meaning: A line showing the outer shape.
To put a name on something.
The area around where you live.
Used for healing or curing illness.

medium.simple_explanation: Having properties that can heal or treat medical conditions.
medium.funny_explanation: Nature's way of saying, 'Here, eat this leaf instead of crying about your scrape.'

examples.text: Some trees in your neighborhood might have great medicinal values.
I tried to claim chocolate has medicinal properties, but my doctor didn't buy it.

words.meaning: Jobs or professions people do.

medium.simple_explanation: The jobs or professions that people do to earn a living.
medium.funny_explanation: The things adults do all day so they can afford to buy us video games and snacks.

examples.text: Many occupations depend on raw materials gathered from the forest.
If 'professional napping' was one of the available occupations, I'd be a billionaire.

words.meaning: Animals living in their natural environment.
The state of being very useful or necessary.
A task used for practice or learning.
Plants found in a particular area.

medium.simple_explanation: The collection of plant life growing in a certain area.
medium.funny_explanation: The giant green blanket the Earth wears to look fancy for the space satellites.

examples.text: The type of vegetation found at high altitudes is different from that on the plains.
The vegetation in my backyard is mostly weeds trying to take over the world.

words.meaning: Part of a group or set.
Natural home of an animal or plant.

medium.simple_explanation: The natural environment where a plant or animal lives.
medium.funny_explanation: An animal's home, but without a TV, a fridge, or a monthly rent bill.

examples.text: Monkeys have a specific habitat in tropical and montane forests.
My natural habitat is usually under a warm blanket with a good book.

words.meaning: Relating to a whole country.
The height of an object above sea level.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The text explains how vegetation changes as one goes higher up in the mountains.
hard.simple_explanation: The height of an object or point in relation to sea level or ground level.
hard.funny_explanation: How high you are on the world's giant invisible ladder.

examples.text: At high altitudes, the air becomes thinner and the vegetation becomes sparse.
At these altitudes, even the clouds look like they're just hanging out in your living room.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like being on the 100th floor of a skyscraper compared to the lobby.
